Freelancer vs Agency vs In-House: How to Hire a Web Developer

Thinking of hiring a web developer? Compare freelancers, agencies and in-house developers, the questions to ask, red flags to avoid and how to brief them.

NM Nipun Mitra ·26 October 2026 ·2 min read

When you need to hire a web developer, the first decision is what kind: a freelancer, an agency or an in-house developer. Each can be the right choice — and each can be an expensive mistake for the wrong project. Here’s how to decide, what to ask, and what to watch out for.

Hiring a freelance web developer

Best for: well-defined websites, landing pages, redesigns and focused features.

  • Pros: usually more affordable, direct communication with the person doing the work, flexible.
  • Cons: limited capacity, and you depend on one person’s availability.

Hiring a web development agency

Best for: large projects needing design, development, content and marketing together.

  • Pros: a full team, project management, more capacity and backup.
  • Cons: higher cost, and you may not speak directly to the developers.

Hiring an in-house developer

Best for: businesses where software is core and changes constantly.

  • Pros: deep knowledge of your business, always available.
  • Cons: salary, benefits and management overhead; one person can’t cover every skill.

Questions to ask before you hire

  1. Can I see live projects similar to mine?
  2. What exactly is included in the quote — design, content, hosting, SEO, training?
  3. How will we communicate, and how often will I see progress?
  4. Who owns the code, the domain and the hosting accounts?
  5. How are changes and extra requests handled?
  6. What happens after launch — bug fixes, updates, support?

Red flags to watch for

  • A fixed price before they’ve asked any questions about your business.
  • No live work to show, only screenshots.
  • Unwillingness to put scope, timeline and payment terms in writing.
  • They keep your domain or hosting in their name.
  • Promises of “guaranteed #1 on Google”.

How to write a brief that gets accurate quotes

  • Your business, your customers and the goal of the project.
  • The pages or features you need — must-haves vs nice-to-haves.
  • Two or three websites you like, and why.
  • Integrations: payments, booking, CRM, delivery, accounting.
  • Your budget range and deadline.

A clear brief helps any developer give you a realistic plan — whether it’s a restaurant website, a booking system or custom software.

Frequently asked questions

Is it better to hire a freelancer or an agency?

Freelancers are usually more affordable and flexible, and great for well-defined projects. Agencies offer a full team and more capacity for large or multi-discipline projects. The right choice depends on scope, budget and how much coordination you can handle.

What should I ask a web developer before hiring?

Ask to see live projects similar to yours, how they communicate and report progress, who owns the code and accounts, how they handle changes, what happens after launch, and what is included in the quote.

How do I write a good brief for a web developer?

Describe your business and goals, your target customers, the main pages or features, examples you like, any integrations, your budget range and your deadline. A clear brief leads to accurate quotes.
